questions.q: Who was the first Viceroy of India under the Government of India Act 1858?
questions.why: After the 1857 revolt, the East India Company's rule ended and Lord Canning became the first Viceroy.

questions.q: The portfolio system in the Indian executive council was introduced by which Viceroy?
questions.why: Introduced via the Indian Councils Act of 1861, allocating specific departments to executive members.

questions.q: Which Viceroy was assassinated in the Andaman Islands by a convict in 1872?
questions.why: Sher Ali Afridi assassinated Lord Mayo during his visit to the convict settlement in Port Blair.

questions.q: The first synchronised census in India took place in 1881 during the tenure of:
questions.why: While the first experimental census was under Mayo (1872), the first complete census was under Ripon.

questions.q: Who passed the controversial Vernacular Press Act of 1878 to gag the Indian press?
questions.why: It was aimed at restricting vernacular newspapers criticizing British policies, later repealed by Ripon.

questions.q: Which Viceroy repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1882?
questions.why: Ripon, known for his liberal policies, restored freedom to the native press.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: A.O. Hume founded the INC while Dufferin was Viceroy. Dufferin initially supported it but later mocked it.

questions.q: The First Factory Act (1881), aimed at improving child labor conditions, was passed by:
questions.why: It restricted working hours for children under 12 and made fencing of dangerous machinery mandatory.

questions.q: Which Viceroy is credited with the introduction of financial decentralization in India?
questions.why: His 1870 resolution gave provincial governments fixed sums to manage local services.

questions.q: The Ilbert Bill controversy, involving the trial of Europeans by Indian judges, occurred under:
questions.why: The European community violently protested against this racial equality measure, forcing Ripon to resign.

questions.q: Who appointed the Hunter Commission in 1882 to review educational progress?
questions.why: The commission focused on primary and secondary education reforms.

questions.q: The Third Anglo-Burmese War (1885), leading to the annexation of Burma, occurred under:
questions.why: Upper Burma was annexed and made a province of British India during his tenure.

questions.q: The Durand Line, separating British India and Afghanistan, was demarcated during the time of:
questions.why: The Durand Commission was set up in 1893 under Viceroy Lansdowne to secure the northwestern frontier.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal (1905) was executed by which Viceroy?
questions.why: Curzon divided Bengal citing administrative convenience, but the real motive was to break nationalist unity.

questions.q: Who passed the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act in 1904?
questions.why: Curzon took great interest in restoring India's architectural heritage and established the ASI directorate.

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement was formally launched in 1905 in response to the policies of:
questions.why: The movement was a direct reaction to Curzon's partition of Bengal.

questions.q: Which Viceroy appointed the Frazer Commission to recommend police reforms?
questions.why: Appointed in 1902, it led to the creation of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).

questions.q: The All India Muslim League was formed in 1906 during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: Formed in Dhaka, it was encouraged by the British to counter the growing influence of the Congress.

questions.q: The Surat Split of the Indian National Congress (1907) happened during the tenure of:
questions.why: The Congress split into Moderates and Extremists over the methods of the Swadeshi movement.

questions.q: Which Act introduced the system of separate electorates for Muslims in India?
questions.why: Lord Minto is known as the 'Father of Communal Electorate' for introducing this divisive policy.

questions.q: The capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911 during the tenure of:
questions.why: The announcement was made during the Delhi Durbar of 1911 by King George V.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy when Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in 1915?
questions.why: Gandhi arrived in January 1915 while Hardinge was still the Viceroy.

questions.q: A bomb was thrown at which Viceroy during his state entry into the new capital of Delhi in 1912?
questions.why: Rash Behari Bose masterminded the Delhi Conspiracy Case, injuring the Viceroy.

questions.q: The Lucknow Pact (1916) between Congress and the Muslim League was signed during the time of:
questions.why: Chelmsford became Viceroy in 1916, overseeing this historic unity agreement.

questions.q: Which Viceroy passed the infamous Rowlatt Act in 1919?
questions.why: The Act allowed imprisonment without trial, leading to nationwide protests and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919) occurred during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: General Dyer ordered the firing on the Baisakhi gathering during Chelmsford's rule.

questions.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Gandhi during the tenure of:
questions.why: Launched in 1920 to protest against the Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh, and the Khilafat wrong.

questions.q: Which British act introduced 'Dyarchy' at the provincial level?
questions.why: It divided provincial subjects into 'Reserved' and 'Transferred' categories.

questions.q: Who was the only Jewish Viceroy of India?
questions.why: Rufus Isaacs, 1st Marquess of Reading, served from 1921 to 1926.

questions.q: The Chauri Chaura incident (1922) which halted the Non-Cooperation Movement happened under:
questions.why: Following the violence, Gandhi called off the movement during Reading's viceroyalty.

questions.q: The Swaraj Party was founded by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru during the tenure of:
questions.why: Formed in 1923 after the failure of the Non-Cooperation movement to contest council elections.

questions.q: The Kakori Train Robbery (1925) was executed by HRA revolutionaries during the time of:
questions.why: Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqulla Khan led the train heist during Reading's tenure.

questions.q: Which Viceroy appointed the Simon Commission in 1927?
questions.why: The all-white statutory commission was appointed to review constitutional reforms.

questions.q: The famous 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was passed in 1929 under:
questions.why: Passed at the Lahore session of INC, protesting against the lack of dominion status.

questions.q: The Dandi March and the Civil Disobedience Movement were launched during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: Gandhi started the salt satyagraha in 1930 during Irwin's tenure.

questions.q: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in which year to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.why: Signed on March 5, 1931, it allowed the Congress to participate in the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy when Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were executed?
questions.why: They were hanged on March 23, 1931, shortly after the Gandhi-Irwin pact.

questions.q: The Second and Third Round Table Conferences were held during the tenure of:
questions.why: Willingdon replaced Irwin in 1931 and adopted strict measures against the renewed Civil Disobedience.

questions.q: Who announced the 'Communal Award' in 1932, creating separate electorates for depressed classes?
questions.why: The British PM announced it, leading to Gandhi's fast unto death and the subsequent Poona Pact.

questions.q: The Poona Pact (1932) was signed between B.R. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi during the time of:
questions.why: It replaced separate electorates for Dalits with reserved seats in joint electorates.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935, which proposed an All India Federation, was passed under:
questions.why: The act granted provincial autonomy and was the last major constitution passed by the British.

questions.q: Provincial elections under the 1935 Act were held in 1937 during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: Congress formed ministries in a majority of provinces but resigned in 1939 over WWII.

questions.q: Which Viceroy unilaterally declared India a belligerent in World War II in 1939?
questions.why: This action without consulting Indian leaders led to the mass resignation of Congress ministries.

questions.q: The 'August Offer' (1940) proposing dominion status was made by:
questions.why: He offered it to secure Indian cooperation in WWII, but both Congress and Muslim League rejected it.

questions.q: The Quit India Movement was launched in 1942 during the tenure of:
questions.why: Following the failure of the Cripps Mission, Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call.

questions.q: The disastrous Bengal Famine of 1943 occurred predominantly during the time of:
questions.why: Millions died due to wartime policies and neglect before Wavell took over and improved relief efforts.

questions.q: Who convened the Simla Conference in 1945 to discuss the reconstruction of the Executive Council?
questions.why: The 'Wavell Plan' failed because Jinnah insisted that only the Muslim League could nominate Muslim members.

questions.q: The INA (Indian National Army) Trials at the Red Fort were held during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: The 1945-46 trials sparked massive nationalist upsurges across the country.

questions.q: The Cabinet Mission (1946) arrived in India during the tenure of:
questions.why: It proposed a weak center and grouping of provinces, which was ultimately unworkable.

questions.q: Direct Action Day (August 16, 1946), leading to massive communal riots, occurred under:
questions.why: Called by the Muslim League, it resulted in the Great Calcutta Killings.

questions.q: Who was the last British Viceroy of India?
questions.why: He was sent in 1947 to oversee the rapid transfer of power and partition of the subcontinent.

questions.q: The 'June 3 Plan', which laid down the framework for India's partition, is also known as the:
questions.why: It officially declared that India would be partitioned into two independent dominions.

questions.q: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.why: India requested him to stay on as Governor-General immediately after independence in 1947.

questions.q: Who was the first and only Indian to become the Governor-General of free India?
questions.why: He succeeded Mountbatten in 1948 and served until the Republic was formed in 1950.

questions.q: Which Viceroy is associated with the doctrine of 'Masterly Inactivity' towards Afghanistan?
questions.why: He strictly avoided interfering in Afghan succession disputes to prevent another costly war.

questions.q: The Royal Titles Act of 1876, conferring the title of 'Empress of India' on Queen Victoria, was passed by:
questions.why: Lytton held a lavish Delhi Durbar in 1877 during a severe famine to announce this.

questions.q: Which Viceroy lowered the maximum age for appearing in the Civil Services Examination from 21 to 19?
questions.why: This deliberately racist move was designed to prevent Indians from entering the elite services.

questions.q: The Statutory Civil Service, nominating Indians of aristocratic families, was created by:
questions.why: Created in 1878, it bypassed the competitive exam but proved highly unsuccessful.

questions.q: Which Viceroy restored the maximum age limit for the Civil Services back to 21 years?
questions.why: Ripon reversed Lytton's oppressive policy to give educated Indians a fair chance.

questions.q: The Kuka Movement in Punjab was suppressed during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: Baba Ram Singh's movement was crushed in 1872 during Northbrook's tenure.

questions.q: Who appointed the Strachey Commission to formulate a comprehensive famine policy?
questions.why: Appointed after the devastating famine of 1876-78, it laid the foundation of the Famine Code.

questions.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1892, introducing the principle of indirect elections, was passed under:
questions.why: It increased the number of non-official members in the legislative councils.

questions.q: Who famously said, 'India is the pivot of our Empire... If the Empire loses any other part of its Dominion we can survive, but if we lose India the sun of our Empire will have set'?
questions.why: Curzon believed deeply in the absolute necessity of India to British imperial power.

questions.q: The setting up of the Department of Agriculture and Commerce was initiated by:
questions.why: Mayo took steps to organize agricultural data and improve farming techniques.

questions.q: Which Viceroy established the Imperial Cadet Corps to provide military training to Indian princes?
questions.why: Curzon created it to satisfy the military ambitions of aristocratic Indian youth.

questions.q: The Munda Uprising led by Birsa Munda (1899-1900) occurred during the tenure of:
questions.why: The Ulgulan (Great Tumult) peaked just as Curzon assumed the viceroyalty.

questions.q: The Indian Universities Act of 1904, increasing government control over colleges, was passed by:
questions.why: Based on the Raleigh Commission, nationalists criticized it as an attempt to crush political dissent in varsities.

questions.q: Which Viceroy survived a bomb attack in Chandni Chowk, Delhi, orchestrated by Rash Behari Bose?
questions.why: He was severely injured but survived the 1912 attack during the capital shift parade.

questions.q: The MacDonnell Commission on famine (1900) was appointed by:
questions.why: It recommended setting up a Famine Commissioner and improving irrigation.

questions.q: The Ghadar Party was formed in San Francisco in 1913 during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: Indian expatriates formed it to trigger a revolution during Hardinge's rule.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy when the tragic Komagata Maru incident occurred in 1914?
questions.why: The Japanese ship carrying Indian immigrants was turned back from Canada, leading to a riot upon return.

questions.q: The establishment of the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in 1916 happened during the tenure of:
questions.why: Madan Mohan Malaviya founded it with the active support of Annie Besant and the GG.

questions.q: The Home Rule League movement by Tilak and Annie Besant started during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: The movement peaked between 1916-1918 demanding self-government within the empire.

questions.q: Which Viceroy appointed the Hunter Committee (Disorders Inquiry Committee) to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy?
questions.why: The committee was a whitewash, leading to widespread anger against Chelmsford.

questions.q: The repeal of the draconian Rowlatt Act was carried out by which Viceroy?
questions.why: Attempting to pacify the masses post-Non-Cooperation, Reading repealed several repressive laws.

questions.q: The Moplah Rebellion (1921) in Kerala broke out during the tenure of:
questions.why: The agrarian revolt took a communal turn and was brutally suppressed by the British.

questions.q: The establishment of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) in 1925 happened under:
questions.why: K.B. Hedgewar founded the organization in Nagpur during Reading's viceroyalty.

questions.q: The Indian Sandhurst Committee (Skeen Committee) regarding the Indianization of the army was appointed by:
questions.why: Appointed in 1925 to investigate the establishment of an Indian military college.

questions.q: The historic bomb explosion in the Central Legislative Assembly by Bhagat Singh (1929) occurred under:
questions.why: They threw the bomb 'to make the deaf hear' protesting against the Public Safety Bill.

questions.q: The martyrdom of Jatin Das after a 63-day hunger strike in Lahore jail happened during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: He fasted demanding political prisoner status in 1929.

questions.q: The Deepavali Declaration of 1929 offering a vague promise of Dominion Status was made by:
questions.why: Irwin made it to placate leaders before the Lahore session, but it lacked a specific timeline.

questions.q: Who was the British Prime Minister during the First Round Table Conference (1930)?
questions.why: He chaired the conferences in London attempting to frame a new constitution.

questions.q: The resumption of the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1932 was met with severe repression by:
questions.why: Unlike Irwin, Willingdon ruthlessly jailed over 80,000 Indians to crush the movement.

questions.q: The foundation of the Congress Socialist Party (1934) occurred during the tenure of:
questions.why: JP Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev, and Minoo Masani formed it within the INC.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 separated which territory from British India?
questions.why: Burma (Myanmar) was administratively separated from India effective 1937.

questions.q: Subhas Chandra Bose formed the Forward Bloc in 1939 during the viceroyalty of:
questions.why: Bose resigned as Congress President due to differences with Gandhi and formed his own faction.

questions.q: The Muslim League's Lahore Resolution (1940) demanding a separate state for Muslims happened under:
questions.why: Drafted by Sikandar Hayat Khan and presented by Fazlul Huq, it formalized the Pakistan demand.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy during the mutiny of the Royal Indian Navy (RIN) in 1946?
questions.why: The naval strike in Bombay severely shook British military confidence in holding India.

questions.q: The Interim Government headed by Jawaharlal Nehru was sworn in during the time of:
questions.why: Sworn in on September 2, 1946, it functioned as a transitional cabinet.

questions.q: Clement Attlee’s declaration setting a deadline of June 1948 for British withdrawal was made while the Viceroy was:
questions.why: Attlee announced it in February 1947, simultaneously replacing Wavell with Mountbatten.

questions.q: The Radcliffe Line demarcating the boundaries of India and Pakistan was finalized under the supervision of:
questions.why: Sir Cyril Radcliffe arrived in July 1947 and finished drawing the borders just days before independence.

questions.q: Who famously declared that the British goal in India was the 'progressive realization of responsible government' in 1917?
questions.why: The August Declaration by the Secretary of State formed the basis for the 1919 reforms.

questions.q: Which Viceroy described the Congress as representing only a 'microscopic minority'?
questions.why: After initially hosting them, Dufferin turned hostile and used this phrase to dismiss the Congress.

questions.q: The White Mutiny by European soldiers protesting the transfer of EIC troops to the Crown occurred under:
questions.why: British soldiers demanded a bounty for the transfer, leading to minor rebellions in 1859.

questions.q: The first High Courts in Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay were established in 1865 during the tenure of:
questions.why: Replacing the old Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats under the Indian High Courts Act 1861.

questions.q: Who created the Indian Forest Department and appointed Dietrich Brandis as its first Inspector General?
questions.why: Lawrence initiated systematic forest conservation in 1864.

questions.q: The famine of Odisha (1866) occurred under the administration of:
questions.why: Over a million died due to strict laissez-faire policies, leading to the Campbell Commission.

questions.q: Which Viceroy organized a grand Durbar in Delhi in 1903 to celebrate the coronation of King Edward VII?
questions.why: Curzon staged the most spectacular and expensive of all Delhi Durbars.

questions.q: The formal integration of princely states post-independence was managed while the Governor-General was:
questions.why: Mountbatten assisted Sardar Patel and V.P. Menon in convincing princes to sign the Instrument of Accession.

questions.q: The Boundary Commission for the partition of Bengal and Punjab was appointed by:
questions.why: He appointed Sir Cyril Radcliffe to head both commissions in June 1947.

questions.q: Which Viceroy is associated with the 'Dickie Bird Plan' which proposed Balkanization of India?
questions.why: His initial 'Plan Balkan' proposed transferring power directly to provinces, which Nehru vehemently rejected.
